clue.text: S ign of cold weather, not special, teeth only ultimately chatter

indicators.note: 'not special' asks for the letter standing for special to be taken away
'ultimately' points to the very end of the word, and 'only' says just that one letter is kept

blocks.note: frost is a sure sign that the weather is cold
S is the abbreviation for special
the final letter of teeth

explanation.surface: Someone in freezing weather notices that their teeth are chattering.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray space in 'S ign' is as the source prints it. FROST loses its S, then the last letter of teeth is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Froth is used figuratively for empty, trivial talk, which is what idle chatter amounts to.

clue.text: Workshop with British work unit occupying fixed floor

indicators.note: the pieces named before this word move in and occupy the inside of the word that follows

blocks.note: a lab is a scientific workshop
B is the abbreviation for British
the erg is the CGS unit of work
fast means firmly fixed, as in stuck fast

explanation.surface: A workshop fitted onto a fixed floor, with some physics of work thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Floor' sits at the end looking like part of a building; here it is the verb meaning to stun. The erg is a small physics unit of work.
explanation.definitionFit: To floor someone is to astonish them so they are lost for words, which is to flabbergast them.

clue.text: Carmen, amateur, useless

blocks.note: read as 'car men': the RAC is the Royal Automobile Club, a motoring organisation
A is the abbreviation for amateur

explanation.surface: A judgment on an amateur production of the opera Carmen: worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Carmen must be split into 'car men'. The RAC is Britain's Royal Automobile Club, a motoring organisation. RACA is a biblical word of contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Raca is a term of reproach from the Gospels meaning worthless or empty-headed, so it serves as an adjective for useless.

clue.text: Barrel lost dry seal

indicators.note: something lost is no longer there, so this letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: B is an abbreviation for barrel
dry in the sense of dull and tedious

explanation.surface: A barrel has lost its seal and dried out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrel' looks like the subject of the sentence; it only supplies the letter B to be removed from BORING.
explanation.definitionFit: An O-ring is a rubber ring used as a gasket to seal a joint between two parts.

clue.text: One in hospital set perchance

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the combination that follows

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital
Chambers gives ply as a bend or set, a direction taken
A is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Someone in a hospital ward wonders whether they are perhaps ready to be discharged.
explanation.walkthrough: A goes inside H plus PLY. Ply as a 'set' or bent is an old Chambers sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Haply is an archaic adverb meaning by chance or perhaps, the same as perchance.

clue.text: Tricky spot right inside shaft

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the word that follows

explanation.walkthrough: SCAPE, an architectural term for the shaft of a column, takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament one has got into, so it is a difficult situation.

clue.text: Very complicated recipes

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters of the following word get rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook's verdict that some recipes are extremely complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very' reads as an intensifier for complicated, but it is the definition, the adjective in 'the very spot'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, very means exact or particular, as in 'the very man', which is what precise means.

clue.text: Plate e.g. duke nicked from club

indicators.note: something nicked from a place has been stolen out of it, so this letter is taken away

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: A piece of silver plate was stolen by a duke from his club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plate' suggests silverware, but it is the River Plate in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plate, or Río de la Plata, is an estuary-river between Argentina and Uruguay, an example of a river.

clue.text: Merge short section of text that's overrunning?

blocks.note: col is the short form of column, a section of printed text
something overrunning goes on beyond its time

explanation.surface: An editor asks to merge a short section of text into one that is running too long.
explanation.definitionFit: To collate is to gather and combine items, such as pages or information, into one ordered whole.

clue.text: Outstanding capital features in Bernini aquatints

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: found running across the end of the first word into the second

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests architecture or a city; here it means the head, and 'outstanding' means protruding.
explanation.definitionFit: Inia, plural of inion, are the bony bumps at the back of the skull, so they stand out on one's head.

clue.text: What may cause traumas at sea?

definitions.text: What may cause traumas at sea?

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about what causes disasters on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides the island, a sumatra is a sudden violent squall in the Strait of Malacca, named after the island, which could well cause trouble on the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a sudden squall at sea, which is what Chambers defines a sumatra to be.

clue.text: Cumbersome peahen trips catching end of bill on spike

the jumbled bird catches a letter and holds it within its own letters

one piece sits on, that is before, the next one in the answer

the final letter of bill
a tine is a spike or prong, as on a fork

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the bird's beak, but only its last letter is used, mixed in with PEAHEN.

clue.text: All upset about tragic playing, requiring tranquillizer

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Both words are jumbled, and the first jumble wraps round the second; 'requiring' links the wordplay to the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Largactil is a trade name for chlorpromazine, a drug used as a major tranquillizer.

clue.text: I am in favour of verse that's ad-lib

pro means for, in favour of

explanation.definitionFit: Improv is improvised performance, made up on the spot without a script, which is what ad-lib means.

clue.text: Protective garb, taking everything into account

second meaning: in total, as a whole

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like advice on choosing workwear; the two halves are separate meanings, one a noun and one an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a protective coat or boiler suit and an adjective meaning comprehensive or total.

clue.text: Gooey stuff, not fat, on rear of univalve

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter
one piece is placed on, that is before, the next

blocks.note: slim means not fat
the final letter of univalve

explanation.walkthrough: A univalve is a mollusc with a single shell, such as a snail, which fits the slime of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Slime is a soft, sticky, gooey substance, such as the mucus a snail secretes.

clue.text: Asian language, no good in north Welsh town

clue.text: Introductory musical section, one in a round

indicators.note: the single letter is placed inside the word that follows

clue.text: Impure metal forming second shower of missiles

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second

clue.text: Bristles? Use half of them wrongly

letters arranged wrongly are in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
them points back to the clue's opening word

explanation.definitionFit: Setules are small bristles or bristle-like hairs, as found on insects and plants.

clue.text: Part of flower Her Madge stuck in bent hatpin

something bent is twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

taken as written

clue.text: Like lardy-cake, or what it's served on, without topping?
